note: #910. Every config key `incus init` receives goes on stdin as a JSON document (YAML 1.2 is a superset of JSON), none on argv, because /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable for the whole create. Proven through the injectable runner, which reads stdin from the same context value runCLI does, plus one real-process test against cat; nothing here proves that Incus accepts the document, which is the runtime conformance leg's job. The stdin route itself was measured on Incus 7.2 on 2026-11-14 with `incus create` (issue comment); feint calls `init`, the CLI's alias of the same cobra command. The YAML readability was measured on 2026-11-15 outside the repository against yaml.v2 v2.4.0, yaml.v3 v3.0.1 and yaml/v4 v4.0.0-rc.3: the escaped document decodes intact under all three and PyYAML 6.0.3, and the unescaped witness (a raw DEL) is refused by all three. Two exclusions in yamlVerbatim carry no mutation, on purpose: U+2028/U+2029, because json.Marshal already escapes them so yamlSafe never sees them raw, and U+FEFF, which the three readers measured kept intact; both are excluded as caution, and a mutation removing either would survive, which this note says rather than leaves to be discovered. Added after the contradictor's pass of 2026-11-15: the cleanup delete runs on context.WithoutCancel, because Start receives the HTTP request's context and the failure being cleaned up may be the client hanging up; the environment shape and the YAML key limit (1024 bytes once encoded, measured on the three readers) are asked by instanceConfigFits at the entry of Start, before anything reaches the runtime. The position mutation moves the guard below the Inspect, and TestAnEnvironmentEntryThatIsNotKeyValueIsRefused requires len(f.calls)==0. Invalid UTF-8 in a user data becomes U+FFFD in the JSON document; that is a limit, written in docs/limits.md, not a mutation here.
